entries.raw_utterance: Let's bump the light up to about eighty-five percent, that should give us plenty of exposure without washing out the field.
Yeah, that's much better. Oh, how was your morning? You look a little tired.
Uhm, just coffee and more coffee, you know how it is. Long call last night.
Okay, bring the scope to zoom level three so we can get a closer look at the appendix and check for any adhesions.
Let's set the insufflator to fourteen millimeters of mercury, and bump the gas flow up to roughly twelve liters per minute. The pressure's a bit low.
Perfect, mhm. Reminds me of that case last month with the unexpected adhesions around the cecum. Anyway, patient's doing fine on the vitals.
Can you roll the table head up about five degrees and drop the height down to ninety-six centimeters? I need a bit more room on the port site.
Alright, unlock the white balance on the scope so I can adjust it manually, and turn on irrigation. Also, engage the safety interlock please, we're about to use the electrocautery near the bowel.
Got it. Uh, the patient's looking stable, right? I hope we're not in for a long one.
Now set the field mode to CavityFocus and lock the white balance back in. Nice, that's better contrast on the camera. The light is a little harsh though, keep the intensity where it is.
Mhm, great. I'll grab the stapler from the tray. Tell me about your kid's soccer game this weekend, did he play well?
Oh, yeah, he scored two goals last week, really excited about that. Uhm, anyway, let me know when you're ready for the specimen bag and we'll wrap this up.
Alright, let's get this started — how's the patient sitting on the table, everything look okay from your end?
Can you bump the main light up to about ninety percent and switch it to CavityFocus for me, please?
Zoom the scope in to level four so we can get a better look at the defect.
Yeah, I caught that — looks like a pretty big inguinal defect on the left side, not tiny.
Hey, did someone call for the extra meds? Uhm, I think we might need a bit more morphine before we go any further.
Let's drop the insufflation target down to eight and bring the gas flow to eight liters a minute — I want a bit more room but not too much pressure.
The patient's blood pressure is holding steady, no worries there.
Unlock the white balance on the scope and turn on irrigation — we're losing contrast and I need some saline flowing.
Tilt the table about ten degrees head-down and lower it to ninety-five centimeters, please.
Okay, let's engage the safety interlock before we start the actual mesh placement.
Great, that's a relief — I was worried about positioning before we locked things in.
Right, let's keep rolling — everyone good?
Alright everyone, ready to get started today?
How was your weekend?
Oh, pretty busy actually, lots of paperwork.
Yeah, same here. Had to redo a few charts.
Good, let's focus on the patient then.
Let's bring the light intensity down to about sixty percent and switch to cavity focus mode.
Can you drop the table height to ninety-five centimeters for me?
Sure, take your time there.
Set insufflator target pressure to fifteen, bring gas flow down to eight, and keep the insufflator active.
Zoom the scope up to level three and make sure white balance stays locked.
Go ahead and start irrigation on the scope now.
Tilt the table back about ten degrees and engage the safety interlock.
Uhm, has anyone seen Dr. Martinez's new watch? It's that big titanium one, pretty slick.
Alright let's crank the light up to about ninety percent and flip it into CavityFocus mode for better exposure down there.
Uhm, wait no - can we zoom the scope to three? I want a closer look at the hernial sac.
Yeah that's perfect, you can see everything clearly now.
I think I heard the cafeteria changed their menu, uhm, not sure if it's any better though.
Pretty nice abdomen, isn't it? Hold that pressure.
Let's go ahead and raise the insufflator target to fifteen millimeters of mercury, and bump the gas flow up to twelve liters per minute.
Let's drop the table down to about ninety-eight centimeters and tilt it five degrees into Trendelenburg.
Can you hand me that Satinsky when you get a sec?
Yeah sure, I'll just grab it from the top tray.
Okay before we start dissection let's engage the safety interlock.
Let's start irrigation through the scope and confirm white balance is locked.
